release.title: calendar
release.notes:
### Recurrence and events

- Recurring events expand in their own time zone, so a weekly 09:00
  meeting stays at 09:00 local time across daylight-saving changes.
  Exceptions and moved occurrences from CalDAV clients are honoured in the
  web views, free/busy and reminders.
- Links to a single occurrence work. Old links of the form {guid}\_{date}
  redirect.
- An occurrence can be edited or deleted on its own, or with all the
  occurrences that follow it.
- Calendars created in the web carry their repeat rule, exceptions and time
  zone over CalDAV and in export.
- The event form refuses an end that is not after the start, and has Show
  as Busy or Free. All-day events default to Free, timed events to Busy.
  All-day events marked Busy block the whole day in free/busy.


### Sharing

- Calendars can be shared at free/busy, read or write level. The recipient
  accepts or declines at /calendar/shares; an email tells them.
- Read and write shares appear in the calendar views under Shared with me
  and as CalDAV collections. With write access the recipient can create,
  edit and delete events, which are stored under the owner.
- The event form shows each local attendee's busy times for the day, for
  attendees whose free/busy the user may see.


### Invitations and scheduling

- Events with attendees send invitations, updates and cancellations by
  email (iMIP) from the web calendar.
- Received invitations show a card in the message view with Accept,
  Tentative and Decline. Replies update the attendee's status on the
  organiser's event.
- CalDAV clients send and answer invitations through the server (RFC 6638
  scheduling). Apple Calendar and Thunderbird stop sending invitation mail
  themselves, so each attendee receives one message.
- Rooms and equipment are accounts that cannot sign in. They accept or
  decline booking requests from their own domain automatically.


### Publishing, subscriptions, tasks and reminders

- A calendar can be published as a read-only iCalendar feed behind a
  random link, with full or busy detail and an optional password.
- External iCalendar feeds can be subscribed to and are refreshed every 6
  hours. The fetcher refuses private and internal network addresses.
- Tasks sync over CalDAV in a Tasks calendar and have a page at /tasks.
  Tasks with a due date appear in the agenda.
- Reminders can be sent by email. A reminder is recorded before it is sent
  and is not sent twice after a restart.


### Mail

- New views: To me, From my contacts and Mailing lists.
- /summary shows unread mail to me, starred mail, invitations awaiting an
  answer and the next seven days. It is the default start page; the inbox
  can be chosen instead in settings.
- The relay passes DSN and SIZE parameters on and sends SMTPUTF8 when a
  message needs it. Bounces and delivery reports to senders outside the
  server are now sent, within the existing limits.


### CalDAV and CardDAV setup

- /.well-known/caldav and /.well-known/carddav answer every request
  method. Apple Calendar and Contacts could not add an account before.
- The Apple configuration profile (/.well-known/mobileconfig) also sets up
  calendar and contacts accounts.
- docs/caldav-carddav.md covers account details, discovery, client setup
  and troubleshooting.


### Upgrade notes

- Upgrade every node before anyone shares a calendar. An older node stores
  sharing commands as plain keys and holds no grants.
- New key: calendar.subscriptions.allow\_private\_networks (default false, a
  restart key).
- The default start page is now the summary page; set the preference to
  inbox to keep the old behaviour.
- Existing shares are migrated once to free/busy grants on the leader.
- Outbound relay now applies go-smtp's command and submission timeouts.
- For discovery by email address, the email domain's own website must
  redirect /.well-known/caldav and /.well-known/carddav to the mail host
  for every request method, or the domain needs the SRV and TXT records the
  admin DNS guide lists.
- Browsers keep the old bongo.js until the asset version changes; reload
  open tabs after upgrading.

Full notes: prds/done/prd-calendar-v0.15.md and prds/verification.md.

patches.title: All Mail, Unread and Starred fixes, tag view actions, macOS shortcuts
patches.notes:
#### All Mail, Unread and Starred

- All Mail, Unread and Starred no longer list messages in Junk or Trash, or
  in any folder below them. Before, All Mail left out only a folder named
  exactly Trash, and Unread and Starred left out nothing.
- All Mail still lists Sent and Drafts.
- Actions in these views act on the message in the row. Before, a message
  was found by its number alone, and numbers repeat between folders. Deleting
  or starring a Sent message from All Mail could change the INBOX message
  with the same number.
- Bulk mark read, mark unread, star and unstar work in these views. They
  failed before.
- A link that names one of these views and a message number, such as an old
  bookmark to /mail/starred/5, now shows Not Found.


#### Tag views

- Star, delete, the bulk actions and opening a message work in a tag view.
  They failed before.


#### Keyboard shortcuts

- ? (shortcut help) and # (move to Trash) work on macOS keyboards.
- The star in a message row can be toggled again after it changes, by click
  or by keyboard.


#### Documentation

- The load test PRD records the results of the connection test (stage 7.4).


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes.

patches.title: notification prompt closes correctly
patches.notes:
#### Web interface

- The desktop notification prompt now closes after enabling notifications or pressing its close button. Its flex layout had overridden the hidden attribute even though the prompt state changed correctly.


#### Documentation

- Record findings from load-test stages 7.1 and 7.3.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes are needed.

patches.title: free the disk space of deleted mail
patches.notes:
#### Mail pipeline

- The spool no longer keeps an envelope for every delivered message. Before,
  each message that finished the pipeline left an envelope file in
  spool/deliver/, and nothing removed it.
- Those envelopes counted as references to the message body. The blob
  garbage collector therefore never deleted the body of a message received
  over SMTP, even after the message was deleted and Trash emptied.
- On the first start, Bongo deletes the envelopes left in spool/deliver/ and
  logs "spool: removed delivered envelopes" with the count.
- The blob garbage collector then frees the bodies of deleted mail. A body is
  deleted when it has been unreferenced on two passes and is older than one
  hour. Passes run every 15 minutes.


#### Documentation

- The load test PRD records the search index size per message measured in
  the first load test run, and a plan to reduce it.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes.
- spool/deliver/ is still created, so a rollback to v0.15.4 works. v0.15.4
  writes envelopes there again until the next upgrade.

patches.title: unified web navigation, live mailbox updates, load test tooling
patches.notes:
#### Navigation

- Every signed-in page has the same application switcher: Mail, Calendar,
  Contacts, Tasks, Settings and Admin, in the same order. It stays in view
  while the sidebar below it scrolls.
- The mail sidebar is grouped into primary mailboxes, More, Views, Folders and
  Tags. More and Views collapse, and the sidebar keeps its scroll position and
  collapsed state between pages.
- Calendar, Contacts, Tasks, Settings, Security, Rules, Tags and Admin use the
  shared sidebar. "Back to Mail" is no longer the only way out of a page.
- On a phone the navigation drawer reports its open state to screen readers.


#### Live mailbox updates

- New mail appears in the open message list without a refresh.
- The update stream follows the folder on screen. It was fixed to INBOX.
- Messages read, moved or deleted in another tab or client update the open
  list. Sidebar unread counts update as mail arrives and as messages are read.
- After a reconnect the list and counts are fetched again.


#### Keyboard triage

- j and k move the selection. Enter opens the selected message.
- e archives, # or Delete moves to Trash, u toggles read and unread. After a
  message leaves the list the next one is selected.
- ? lists every shortcut. Shortcuts do nothing while typing in a field or the
  composer.


#### Web interface fixes

- A failed save, move or delete shows an error. Before, some failures were
  silent.
- The desktop notification prompt no longer blocks the page. It can be
  dismissed and does not cover controls on a phone.
- The desktop notification icon loads.
- The calendar event editor has a page header and its actions stay visible on
  a phone.
- Week and Day views open scrolled to an hour before the current time when
  they show today, and to 07:00 otherwise.
- Unpublishing a calendar, issuing a new feed link and removing a feed
  password ask for confirmation.
- Settings tabs work with the arrow keys and show when more tabs are off
  screen.
- Admin tables scroll sideways on a phone instead of cutting off columns.
- Focus returns to the control that opened a dialog or menu when it closes.
- Animation is reduced when the system asks for reduced motion.


#### Server metrics

- New Prometheus metrics: open per-user databases and evictions, search index
  backlog and open indexes, Raft apply time and commit lag, FSM apply time,
  Pebble compactions, write stalls and WAL sync time, blob count and bytes,
  blob garbage collection passes, snapshot time, and per-protocol connections
  and command time.
- Process CPU, memory and open files, and Go runtime metrics, are exported.


#### Configuration

- storage.max\_open\_user\_dbs sets how many per-user SQLite databases stay open
  (default 256, 1 to 16384). Read at startup.
- telemetry.pprof serves CPU and heap profiles on the loopback control
  listener only. Off by default. Read at startup.


#### Load testing

- scripts/loadgen generates SMTP, IMAP, POP3, CalDAV and CardDAV traffic,
  bulk-loads a fresh data directory, samples server metrics and writes a
  report. It refuses production domains.
- docs/load-testing.md is the runbook. deploy/loadtest.example.hcl is the
  test server configuration.
- The first test run is in progress. Results will be published separately.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes are needed. Both new settings are optional.

patches.title: app passwords
patches.notes:
#### App passwords

- An app password is a per-device credential for IMAP, POP3, SMTP submission,
  CalDAV and CardDAV. It never signs in to the web interface.
- Each password has 24 letters. Bongo shows it once and stores only a hash.
- Settings, Security lists each password with its label, creation date and last
  used date. A user can hold up to 10.
- Creating a password needs the account password, and a code with 2FA on.
- A successful app password login forgives no failed guesses at the account
  password.
- A user name with the shape of an app password is not logged.
- Revoking a password refuses its next login and ends the IMAP, POP3 and SMTP
  sessions it opened on their next command.
- Change password has a box, ticked by default, that also revokes all app passwords.
- An admin can revoke all of a user's app passwords.


#### Add a device

- Add a device shows a new app password beside the server settings. These match
  the autoconfig documents.
- Apple devices can download a personal profile with Mail, Calendar, Contacts and
  Reminders set up. The profile is unsigned, so the device shows Not Verified.
- A QR code holds a one-time link for a phone. The link expires after 5 minutes
  and works once.


#### Require app passwords

- An account with 2FA and at least one app password can turn on Require app
  passwords. IMAP, POP3, SMTP submission, CalDAV and CardDAV then refuse the
  account password.
- Turning it on ends sessions opened with the account password.
- The switch is offered at the end of 2FA enrolment and on the Security page.


#### Documentation

- docs/caldav-carddav.md, docs/sendmail.md, docs/walkthrough.md and SECURITY.md
  cover app passwords and the switch.
- docs/design/from-nmap-to-one-binary.md records the move from NMAP agents to one
  binary.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes.
- Nothing changes for an account until its owner creates an app password or turns
  on the switch.
- Upgrade every node together. An earlier binary stores the app password touch and
  link commands as literal keys, ignores the switch and refuses app passwords.


#### Known limits

- The Apple profile and QR link have not been checked on real devices.

Full notes: prds/done/prd-app-passwords-v0.15.3.md and prds/verification.md.

patches.title: web UI fixes
patches.notes:
#### Calendar

- The calendar settings page uses the shared page, card, field and button
  styles, in light, dark and mobile.
- The calendar sidebar shows coloured dots and themed checkboxes. Import is
  one button. The month title in the mini calendar is readable in the light
  theme.
- The week and day views show the weekday and date above each column, with
  today highlighted. A header links to that day.
- The event form follows the theme. Its controls were white in dark mode.
- The calendar invitations page uses the shared page and card styles.
- The result of an import is shown after the import.


#### Tasks and Apple Reminders

- An account with no calendar that holds tasks gets the Tasks calendar the
  next time it opens a calendar page or a CalDAV client lists its calendars.
  This calendar sits outside the limit of 5 calendars per user.
- The placeholder name DEFAULT\_TASK\_CALENDAR\_NAME from Apple Reminders is
  stored as "Tasks". A list already created with that name keeps it.


#### Admin

- The product name is readable on the admin header. The admin footer and the
  link back to mail are styled.


#### Development

- make seed creates tasks.
- make ui-shots also covers calendar invitations, the event form and tasks.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes.
- An account with 4 event calendars and no Tasks calendar has one calendar
  fewer available after the upgrade, because Tasks is added.

Full notes: prds/done/prd-ui-fixes-v0.15.2.md and prds/verification.md.

patches.title: calendar fixes
patches.notes:
#### CalDAV and CardDAV

- CalDAV clients can create calendars and lists (MKCALENDAR and extended
  MKCOL). A list created in Apple Reminders or Thunderbird holds tasks.
- A calendar can be deleted in the web or from a CalDAV client, with its
  events, tasks, shares and published feed. Tasks, the default calendar and
  the last event calendar cannot be deleted.
- A missing CalDAV object answers 404, not 500.
- CalDAV and CardDAV ETags are quoted once, so updates with If-Match are
  accepted. Events created in the web have a content ETag over CalDAV.
  Clients fetch every contact, and every event created in the web, once
  after the upgrade.
- Windows time-zone names, as Outlook sends them, resolve through the CLDR
  table. Such events were stored at 1970 before.
- Events are filed only in calendars that exist.


#### Calendars

- A calendar can be created in the web, with a name, a colour and
  optionally tasks. A user owns at most 5 calendars, Personal and Tasks
  included; the limit applies in the web, over CalDAV and to subscriptions.
- "This and following" no longer leaves an empty series behind when the
  first occurrences were deleted.


#### Tasks

- Tasks in calendars shared with the user appear, read-only, in /tasks and
  the agenda.
- Recurring tasks appear at every occurrence. Overdue open tasks appear on
  today's row.
- A due date before the start is refused.


#### Invitations and scheduling

- Updates carry a higher SEQUENCE. Title and description changes are sent
  to attendees.
- No invitations or cancellations are sent for events entirely in the past.
  An all-day event is past from midnight in the user's time zone.
- CalDAV clients schedule single occurrences and attendees invited to one
  occurrence only.
- Deleting an invitation in a CalDAV client declines it.
- A reply covering several occurrences is applied to all of them.
- The invitation card shows the user's own answer. A user invited only at
  an alias they cannot send from is told the organiser will not be told.
- Rooms and equipment answer bookings for single occurrences. Booking mail
  is no longer kept in the resource's inbox.


#### Sharing and reminders

- Pending calendar shares expire after 30 days. A user can leave a calendar
  shared with them.
- Browser reminders fire once.
- Dates in reminder mail and the agenda follow the user's language.


#### Mail and web

- The To me, From my contacts and Mailing lists views moved to
  /mail/view/..., so folders with those names are reachable.
- "Unread mail to me" on the summary page lists unread mail only.
- Display names containing a comma, including encoded non-ASCII names, are
  no longer split.
- Status messages show only fixed, translated texts; a link can no longer
  put its own text in a message.
- The recovery-code warning is shown on the inbox.
- The Apple configuration profile has per-user identifiers, so two users of
  one domain can install theirs on one device.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration changes.
- Links to /mail/to-me, /mail/from-contacts and /mail/lists change to
  /mail/view/...; the old paths are not redirected.
- Status links carrying free text in ?flash= no longer show it.

Full notes: prds/active/prd-calendar-fixes-v0.15.1.md and
prds/verification.md. docs/caldav-carddav.md covers creating and deleting
calendars.

release.title: mail delivery and rules
release.notes:
### Postmaster and submission

- postmaster@ and abuse@ resolve on every hosted domain: to the domain
  owner, else to smtp.postmaster\_account, else to the catch-all. Without a
  target, RCPT gets 550 5.1.1 and startup lists the domains concerned.
- queue.bounce\_copy\_postmaster (default off) sends a headers-only copy of
  each bounce to postmaster@ the sender's domain.
- Implicit-TLS submission on port 465 is on when smtp.tls is set.
  Autoconfig, Autodiscover, the Apple profile and the admin DNS guide list
  465 first, only when the SMTP listeners start.
- An RCPT to an unknown local part on a hosted domain, alias domains
  included, is refused with 550 5.1.1. An authenticated session used to
  relay it and the sender received a bounce later.


### Vacation and rules

- Vacation replies at /settings/vacation, with RFC 3834 loop protection,
  one reply per sender per interval (1 to 30 days, default 7) and at most
  100 replies per user per hour.
- A rule can have up to 10 actions. flag, mark read and copy now work as
  named; copy no longer moves. Spam stays in Junk.
- New rules continue to the next rule after a match. Existing rules are
  migrated to stop after a match, so they behave as before. The migration
  also runs on a node that becomes leader later.
- Rules can match any condition instead of all. New conditions: MIME type
  of any part, and any header by name.


### Queue, DSN and storage

- queue.max\_lifetime (default 5 days, was about 17 hours),
  queue.max\_retry\_interval (1 hour) and queue.concurrency (5).
- SMTP DSN parameters RET, ENVID, NOTIFY and ORCPT are accepted and
  honoured for local senders, including delay reports
  (queue.delay\_warning\_after, default 4 hours). Reports to external senders
  are not sent yet.
- Below storage.min\_free\_mb (default 1024) the server refuses new mail,
  IMAP APPEND, uploads and DAV writes with a temporary error, and the admin
  page shows a banner.


### Domains, web mail and CLI

- Domain aliasing: mail to user@alias.example is delivered to
  user@example.com. A domain with alias domains cannot be deleted.
- Archive and Unarchive in the message view, the bulk toolbar, the e key
  and a left swipe on a phone, including from Starred and other virtual
  views. A left swipe used to move the message to Trash. IMAP clients see
  \\Archive on the Archive mailbox.
- Reply to List. Replies follow Reply-To. Your own addresses are removed
  from To and Cc; Reply on your own sent message addresses its original
  recipients.
- bongo sendmail, a sendmail-compatible submission client for cron and
  scripts (docs/sendmail.md).
- bongo user list, bongo domain list and bongo alias list, as a table or
  JSON.


### Upgrade notes

- Upgrade every node before setting any new key (smtp.postmaster\_account,
  smtp.submissions\_port, queue.\*, storage.min\_free\_mb) or creating an alias
  domain, a multi-action rule or a match-any rule. An older node refuses
  the new keys and ignores the new rule fields.
- Publish port 465 before deploying, or set smtp.submissions\_port = 0.
- Check the 1 GiB storage.min\_free\_mb default against the free space on
  the data volume.
- A configured smtp.tls certificate that fails to load now stops startup.
- Browsers keep the old bongo.js until the asset version changes; reload
  open tabs after upgrading.

Full notes: prds/done/prd-mail-delivery-v0.14.md and prds/verification.md.

patches.title: postmaster startup report
patches.notes:
#### Fixes

- The startup warning about postmaster@ and abuse@ now names a domain only
  when one of those addresses does not resolve. Explicit addresses, legacy
  aliases and catch-alls count. In v0.14.0 it checked only the domain owner
  and smtp.postmaster\_account, so it named domains whose postmaster@ was
  delivered by an alias and said their mail was refused.
- The warning now reads "domains where postmaster@ or abuse@ does not
  resolve". Log filters that matched the v0.14.0 text need updating.


#### Upgrade notes

- No configuration change. Delivery is unchanged; only the warning differs.

Full notes: prds/done/prd-mail-delivery-v0.14.md.

release.title: web UI rebuild
release.notes:
### Web UI

- Every screen is rebuilt to the Bongo Mail design: new shell with top bar,
  account menu and grouped sidebar; design tokens, Geist fonts and one icon
  set; light and dark mode, including the login and other public pages.
- Mailbox list shows previews, attachment markers, header counts and a bulk
  toolbar. Message and thread view has a quick reply. Compose uses recipient
  pills and a drop zone for attachments.
- Calendar has an agenda view and shows times in the user's time zone
  throughout. Contacts, rules, settings, security, tags, Junk and admin
  (KPI cards, tables, status pills) follow the same layout.
- No emoji remain in the templates.


### Fixes from operator testing

- Tagging works from the message view, the bulk toolbar and the context
  menu. Typed tag names are folded into stored form ("My Tag" becomes
  "my-tag"); a rejected tag shows an error instead of closing the picker.
- The rule editor, the contact editor and the calendar show/hide checkbox
  work under the Alpine CSP build.
- Sidebar unread counts update live when messages are read or arrive.
- "Create filter" in a message's More and context menus opens a new rule
  matching the sender.
- Tag colour swatches are announced by colour name.


### Correctness

- SQLite busy\_timeout and WAL mode apply to every pooled connection, not
  only the first; a contended index write now waits instead of failing with
  SQLITE\_BUSY.
- An agent cancelled during registration shuts down cleanly.


### Operations

- golang.org/x/net updated to v0.62.0 for two html advisories.
- Templates are generated with templ v0.3.1001.
- Assets are cache-busted by commit hash; reload open tabs after upgrading.

Full notes: prds/active/prd-ui-rebuild-v0.13.md.

patches.title: reminder checker crash fix
patches.notes:
#### Stability

- The server no longer panics in the calendar reminder checker. The
  checker closed a storage iterator twice. Storage reuses closed
  iterators, so the second close could break another scan in progress
  and stop the server with "index out of range" in mergingIter.Close.
  The fault was present since v0.1.0 and occurred after several hours of
  running. A repeated close of a storage iterator is now a no-op.

patches.title: the app is named bongo
patches.notes:
#### Naming

- The server binary and CLI are named bongo. The release zips are named
  bongo\_\<version\>\_linux\_amd64.zip and bongo\_\<version\>\_linux\_arm64.zip.
- The container image runs /usr/local/bin/bongo.
- The systemd unit is bongo.service.
- The default data and log directories are /var/lib/bongo and
  /var/log/bongo.
- Protocol greetings, the Received-SPF header, log messages, the
  self-signed certificate and the calendar PRODID use the name Bongo.

patches.title: domain administration fixes, Linux binaries, documentation
patches.notes:
#### Security

- Only global administrators can delete a domain. A domain administrator
  could previously delete a domain they administer with a direct request,
  although the web UI did not offer it.


#### Mail

- A disabled domain refuses all inbound mail. SMTP answers 550 5.1.1 for
  every address on it, including aliases and the catch-all. Accounts and
  stored mail are kept; re-enabling the domain restores delivery. Previously
  disabling a domain only removed it from client autoconfiguration.


#### Releases

- Each version tag now publishes a GitHub release with Linux binaries for
  amd64 and arm64, a SHA256SUMS file, and these notes. The zips include
  LICENSE and THIRD\_PARTY\_NOTICES.md.


#### Documentation

- The walkthrough and development guide describe the rebuilt web UI.
- Deployment, installation, configuration, import, clustering and
  multi-domain documentation was checked against the code and corrected.
- The edge and agent server roles are documented as incomplete. Use the
  server role.
- Dev mode serves the web UI over plain HTTP. make seed, make validate and
  make ui-test-setup now work against a dev server.

Full notes: prds/active/prd-ui-rebuild-v0.13.md (section 8.2).

patches.title: web UI fixes from operator testing
patches.notes:
#### Mail view

- Two-pane shows the message list above the reading pane; three-pane shows
  them side by side. The two layouts previously looked the same.
- In both pane layouts a message opens in the reading pane instead of
  replacing the whole view. A click anywhere on a message row opens it.
- In the pane layouts the list and the reading pane scroll separately.


#### Keyboard

- In the pane layouts j and k open the highlighted message after a 300 ms
  pause. Holding the key moves through the list without marking every
  message read.
- d moves the highlighted message to Trash. In Trash, d does nothing.
- d, r and drag-and-drop act on the mailbox on screen after sidebar
  navigation. Previously they could act on a message with the same UID in
  the previously loaded mailbox.


#### Fixes

- Deleting, moving or marking spam in a subfolder such as INBOX/Important
  returns to that subfolder instead of showing "Invalid UID".
- Pages load in dark mode without a light flash when the OS or the saved
  preference is dark.


#### Branding

- The top bar and login page show the swoosh from the original Bongo project
  logo.

Assets are cache-busted by commit hash; reload open tabs after upgrading.

Full notes: prds/active/prd-ui-rebuild-v0.13.md (US-024 to US-029).

release.title: hardening release
release.notes:
### Security

- /internal/\* control routes move to a loopback control listener,
  server.control\_addr (default 127.0.0.1:8081); the web port answers 404.
  The bongo-go CLI defaults --http-addr to it.
- Bounces of forwarded mail are relayed only for SPF-pass or
  authenticated senders.
- SMTP DATA and BDAT refuse a body more than a tenth plus 1 KiB over the
  declared SIZE (552 5.3.4).
- CalDAV and CardDAV share a 64 MiB budget for request bodies in flight.
- Send-as verification no longer reveals whether an address is taken; at
  most 20 pending claims per user; claims are removed with the address
  or domain; concurrent correct codes yield one owner.
- IMAP, SMTP and POP3 fail closed when the account state cannot be read.
- A redirect-listener bind failure stops startup; a web Serve error after
  ready shuts the node down.
- Uploads spool to disk above 8 MiB; the mailbox import streams messages
  and checks quota first.


### Correctness

- SMTP writes one envelope per local recipient, so one recipient's rules
  no longer file or drop another's copy.
- A retried web send no longer duplicates (send ID; 409 on changed
  content). Compose tabs opened before the upgrade must be reloaded.
- Calendar export keeps its time zones; all-day reminders use the owner's
  zone; the month grid shows neighbouring months' all-day events.
- Compose messages are translated (de, es, fr).


### Operations

- Config validation refuses colliding or out-of-range listener ports and a
  server with a wildcard bind and no advertise or cluster bind address,
  at startup and on hot reload.
- Built with Go 1.27.3; raft 1.8.0 and memberlist 0.7.0 (protocol
  versions unchanged); chi updated past three advisories.
- The repository is licensed AGPL-3.0; the web UI links to the source
  (web.source\_url).

Full notes: prds/active/prd-hardening-v0.12.md, section 8.2.

Phase B of the hardening PRD: agent role and cluster transport security.

- Internal requests sign with the effective session secret; agent-role SMTP
  verifies SRS recipients; agent antispam no longer skips DMARC on
  unverifiable trust flags.
- New cluster.bind\_addr; Raft and gossip never bind server.bind\_addr.
- Raft with peers requires cert, key and CA, verifies peers, no plaintext.
- Agent gRPC servers and clients use mutual TLS and bind the cluster address.
- Blob sync and cluster join move to a mutual TLS peer listener
  (cluster.peer\_port, default 8302) on nodes with peers.

Upgrade notes: a server with a non-loopback advertise\_addr needs cluster
cert, key and ca\_file; server.bind\_addr 0.0.0.0 without advertise\_addr no
longer starts; role agent needs the agent\_server.tls files; nodes with peers
must be upgraded together. Production (role server, single node, loopback
advertise) is unaffected.

patches.notes:
IMAP subscriptions, correct sequence numbering, and a working cluster status.

feat(imap): implement folder subscriptions

  Subscribe and Unsubscribe were no-ops and List read only ReturnStatus, so
  LSUB returned every mailbox rather than the subscribed subset, \\Subscribed
  was never emitted, and unsubscribing a folder did not stick.

  State lives on MailboxMeta as "unsubscribed", inverted deliberately. Every
  mailbox already on disk has no such field and decodes as the zero value; with
  "subscribed" that value is false, which would unsubscribe every folder for
  every user on upgrade. Inverted, it means still-subscribed, so this release
  changes nothing for existing mailboxes until someone explicitly
  unsubscribes.

  SUBSCRIBE applies through a synthetic Raft command rather than writing back a
  whole MailboxMeta, which would race a delivery and reset uid\_next, handing the
  next message a duplicate UID.

fix(imap): number EXPUNGE and SEARCH from the client's view

  Sequence numbers were computed from the server's message list. They are only
  meaningful relative to what the client has been told, and the two diverge as
  soon as another connection removes a message between the client's last update
  and the command -- at which point EXPUNGE tells the client to drop the wrong
  message.

fix(cmd): authenticate bongo-go cluster status

  It called http.Get unsigned against an endpoint behind RequireInternalAuth, so
  it returned 401 on every node with web.session\_secret set. It worked only on a
  dev node with no secret, which is where nobody needs it.

Outbound mail fails fast when its body is gone.

fix(queue): bounce immediately when the message body is gone

  handleFailure treats every error as worth retrying and only bounces once
  maxAttempts is spent. A message enqueued before the 2026-08-30 blob-GC
  incident therefore spent seven days cycling through attempts that each failed
  identically: its body blob no longer exists, so the ninth attempt fails
  exactly as the first did.

  handlePermanentFailure bounces without consuming the remaining retries. It
  fires only on store.ErrNotFound, because the distinction that matters is "the
  body is gone" against "the blob store is unwell" -- an I/O error, a
  permissions problem, or a store still starting are transient and keep their
  backoff. Both read paths are covered, including RawMessageBytes for split
  messages where a missing attachment is equally unrecoverable.

  Nine wasted attempts is the smaller cost. The larger one is that the DSN the
  sender received blamed delivery, when the body is gone and resending is the
  only remedy. The bounce now says so.

IMAP clients are told about new mail outside IDLE.

fix(imap): tell clients about new mail outside IDLE

  session.Poll returned nil with the comment "no-op, we use IDLE". go-imap runs
  Conn.poll after every command in the authenticated or selected state, and that
  is how a server delivers untagged EXISTS and EXPUNGE to a client polling with
  NOOP. Returning nil meant the only way any client learned about new messages
  was IDLE, and only while idling on that exact mailbox.

  Observed: a message appended to a user's Sent folder stored correctly, but
  Thunderbird did not display it until the client was restarted, which forced a
  fresh SELECT. Thunderbird idles on INBOX and polls other folders with NOOP.

  The fix needs two baselines. cachedMsgs is the sequence-number working set that
  handlers refresh freely -- Fetch, Store, Search, Copy and Move all overwrite it
  at the top of the handler, and the poll runs after the handler returns, so
  diffing against it destroys the pending EXISTS rather than deferring it.
  reportedUIDs records what the client has actually been sent.

  The baseline moves wherever the client is genuinely told something: Select,
  Poll, Idle, Expunge and Move. Expunge and Move write untagged EXPUNGEs
  themselves, and omitting them would leave the next poll re-sending a sequence
  number the client has already renumbered against, dropping a message it should
  have kept.

  Expunges are written highest sequence number first, since each renumbers those
  after it, and are withheld when allowExpunge is false because FETCH, STORE and
  SEARCH must not emit them mid-command.

Known and unchanged: Subscribe and Unsubscribe are still no-ops, and List
ignores SelectSubscribed, so LSUB returns every mailbox rather than the
subscribed subset. Every folder is effectively always subscribed.

Raft snapshots actually happen, and the log finally truncates.

fix(cluster): apply every raft tuning value, and stop the log growing forever

  The production node had not snapshotted since 2026-08-23. Every restart
  restored a two-week-old snapshot, rebuilt derived indexes for the state as of
  that date, and warned for each message whose blob had since been collected --
  warnings that accumulate permanently, one per delete-then-GC cycle. It also
  feeds the accepted first-delivery stall (B12), which scales with log size.

  Three causes, only one of them tuning.

  snapshot\_interval was parsed, defaulted, documented and set in the production
  config, and never assigned to raft.Config. A settable key with no destination
  is invisible: nothing downstream changes, so no behavioural test can see it.

  TrailingLogs was not configurable, and raft's own default of 10240 exceeds
  this project's snapshot\_threshold default of 8192. Neither number is wrong
  alone, but together the threshold is inert -- a snapshot fires and then
  retains more entries than triggered it, so the log never truncates. It is now
  configurable, and an inverted pairing is refused at startup with the reason in
  the error. A node on the defaults is warned rather than refused, because
  changing those defaults would alter behaviour for existing deployments.

  The threshold was also far too high for a node delivering roughly five
  messages a day. Code defaults are unchanged; only the production config is
  tuned, to 256 with 128 trailing.

  Adds "bongo-go cluster snapshot" to force one on the leader, since a stale
  snapshot cannot otherwise be cleared without waiting for the threshold.

Known issue, not fixed here: "bongo-go cluster status" cannot authenticate
against a node with web.session\_secret set. It calls http.Get unsigned against
an endpoint behind RequireInternalAuth and returns 401.

Tooling to see and act on mail whose body blob was lost.

feat(admin): report and purge mail whose body blob is gone

  Eight messages carry MailMeta records whose raw\_message blob no longer exists,
  left by the 2026-08-30 blob-GC incident. They appear in no per-user SQLite
  index, which proves nothing: that row is written during indexing, and indexing
  is what fails on a missing body.

  Adds FindDanglingMail and DeleteDanglingMail, the /internal/mail/dangling and
  /internal/mail/purge-dangling endpoints behind internal auth, and the
  "bongo-go mail dangling" / "mail purge-dangling --confirm" commands, mirroring
  the existing orphaned-address repair.

  The report lists every MailboxMessage entry referencing each GUID, which is
  what distinguishes orphaned metadata from a live message sitting in a mailbox.
  Deletion removes those entries too, and before the MailMeta: the sequence is
  several Raft commands and is not atomic, and this order leaves orphaned
  MailMeta on an interruption -- which sweepOrphanedMail already reclaims --
  rather than a mailbox entry pointing at nothing, which nothing cleans up.

  Each blob is re-checked immediately before its record is removed, since blob
  sync can pull one back from a peer between the scan and the delete.

  Also corrects a false claim in v0.6.25's 14.5 work. It said a MailboxMessage
  decoded as a MailMeta fails proto.Unmarshal on a wire-type clash, and that a
  user could therefore disable blob GC by naming a mailbox "mail". The decode
  does not fail; protobuf-go skips a wire-type mismatch on a known field number
  as an unknown field. That denial-of-service never existed. The structural key
  parse remains correct for the plainer reason that unmarshal success is not
  evidence a value is the type you expected.

This release ships the report. No purge has been run.

Blob GC reference integrity: the fixes for the 2026-08-30 mail-body loss.

blob-gc is the only component that deletes blobs, and blobs are content-addressed
and shared, so one missed reference loses that content for every holder with no
undo. On 2026-08-30 a sweep deleted 17 blobs, two of which were still referenced.
An audit found eight gaps. This release fixes all of them.

blob\_gc must stay "dryrun" until the candidate lists produced by this build have
been reviewed on real data. This release makes that review possible; it does not
authorise re-enabling deletion.

fix(agent): re-validate blob GC candidates immediately before deleting

  The minAge grace assumed a blob's mtime tracks its most recent write, but
  BlobStore.Put early-returns without touching the file when the hash already
  exists. A deduplicated write therefore keeps the ORIGINAL mtime, so a blob that
  becomes referenced again during the reference scan is simultaneously absent from
  the snapshot, older than the cutoff, and a two-pass candidate. Both existing
  guards miss it, and the stamped-message redelivery path makes it deterministic.
  Candidates are now re-checked against a fresh reference set immediately before
  deletion, inside deleteSweptBlobs so nothing can reach a delete without it.

fix(agent): count queued outbound attachments as referenced blobs

  Attachment-dedup splits an outbound message into a skeleton plus separate
  attachment blobs, which the queue worker reassembles before relaying. Only the
  skeleton was referenced, so the GC reclaimed the attachments and the message
  relayed with them missing. The queue entry stayed healthy throughout, so this
  damaged outbound mail without leaving any evidence.

fix(agent): parse mail keys structurally, then fail loudly on bad records

  The mail scan matched a "/mail/" substring, which a user could trip by creating
  an IMAP mailbox named "mail". proto.Unmarshal failures were then silently
  skipped, dropping references. Fixed in that order deliberately: making unmarshal
  fatal first would have let any user disable the GC node-wide.

fix(agent): do not carry blob GC candidates across a failed pass

  Both error paths returned the previous candidate set, so it survived an
  arbitrary run of failed passes and "two consecutive passes" stopped meaning two
  consecutive good ones.

fix(agent): scan the spool twice so a released message keeps its body

  An admin releasing a message from quarantine moves it backward through the
  directory order the scan reads, so a release landing mid-scan appeared in no
  listing at all and its body looked unreferenced.

feat(agent): log every blob a sweep reclaims, with size and mtime

  The incident left "candidates:17 deleted:17" and nothing else, so the hashes
  were unrecoverable and attribution meant decoding spool envelopes by hand. Both
  modes now log per-blob detail at Info: a deleting pass is the one whose record
  cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

test(agent): fail when a blob-bearing proto field escapes the reference set

  Twice a field that pins a blob was missing from the scan. A descriptor walk now
  requires every blob-bearing proto field to be explicitly classified, so a third
  recurrence fails the build instead of production.

Two data races in the Raft FSM, and the per-user data leak behind the
ghost-mailbox incident.

fix(cluster): synchronise FSM dependency injection against the apply loop

  Agent.Run injects the search indexer, blob syncer, notifier and derived-index
  queue into the FSM after handing it to Raft, so the apply goroutine read those
  fields while Run was still writing them. This fires on any restart that
  applies Raft entries during startup - i.e. every restart with a non-empty log.
  StartIndexer's check-then-assign was also a double-start window: two callers
  could each create a queue, orphaning the first worker. All four fields are now
  guarded and read through accessors.

fix(admin): reclaim per-user data left behind by account deletion

  DeleteUser removed /user/{id}/\* and the users row but neither the per-user
  metadata database nor the search index, so every deleted account leaked both.
  That leak is what let delivery keep succeeding into a deleted account's
  mailbox. Adds the cascade, plus an orphan-GC sweep that reclaims /user/{id}/
  trees with no users row and no profile - which also unpins the blobs those
  keys were holding.

chore(ci): stop running every workflow twice per pull request

fix(admin): delete a user's address-index records when the user is deleted

Deleting a user left its /system/address/ records behind. Because
RecipientResolver consults the address index ahead of aliases, the users
table and the catch-all, a stale record outranked any alias later created
for the same address and resolved mail to the deleted account - delivered
into an unreachable mailbox, neither bounced nor visible.

Adds the DeleteUser cascade, plus 'bongo-go address orphans' and
'bongo-go address repair' to find and remove existing stale records.

- Blob/orphan GC now announces its configured mode at startup, so a
  blob\_gc change is verifiable from the logs instead of being silent.
- Composite antispam processor merges the losing backend's reasons
  rather than discarding them (B14).
- deploy: blob\_gc returned to "on"; grafana dashboard removed with the
  observability stack.
- ci: golangci-lint pinned to v2.13.2.

Returns blob\_gc to "on" now that collectReferencedBlobs scans all five
spool directories, and is the first release published under the
bongo-project/bongo name.

patches.title: - data-loss fixes, DAV correctness, tenant isolation
patches.notes:
Contains fixes for three ways live mail could be destroyed, one of which
was observed in production on 2026-08-27. Deploying this is what allows
storage.blob\_gc to be returned to "on"; until then the running config
must stay at "dryrun", and note that dryrun does NOT protect the
quarantine deletion paths.

Data loss

- Blob GC never counted the on-disk spool. A blob referenced only by a
  spool envelope -- quarantined mail awaiting review, or anything
  deferred past the one-hour grace -- was reclaimed while the envelope
  survived. Observed symptom: an outbound forward failing with "blob not
  found", because deliver.go reuses the spool envelope's BlobHash when
  it enqueues a forward. Content in that state is unrecoverable.
- Quarantine deletion destroyed other users' mail. Blobs are
  content-addressed and shared, so quarantined spam has the same hash as
  any byte-identical copy delivered elsewhere -- the normal case for a
  broadcast message. All three paths did it, including the unattended
  hourly auto-purge, which no configuration setting disables.
- Queue retry, bounce and retry-now were two Raft commands each: delete
  the old key, put the new one. A crash or rejection between them left
  the message at neither key. Now one composite command applied in a
  single Pebble batch.

Security and correctness

- The Global Address List could not be scoped: any authenticated user
  could enumerate every address of every tenant through compose
  autocomplete. Now restricted to the caller's own domain.
- IMAP EXAMINE was not read-only. STORE, EXPUNGE and MOVE all mutated a
  mailbox the client had been told was read-only; MOVE emptied it.
- CalDAV/CardDAV ignored If-Match and If-None-Match entirely, so
  concurrent edits silently last-write-wins. ETags were also
  second-resolution, which had to be fixed first or the preconditions
  would have protected nothing.
- Mixed permanent and transient relay outcomes re-sent to and re-bounced
  permanently-failed recipients on every attempt, up to ten duplicate
  DSNs per address.

Other

- Received mail bodies are now indexed, so body search works for mail
  you received and not only mail you sent.
- Tagging a message no longer deletes its indexed body.
- Calendar events with an unparseable RRULE are shown as a single
  occurrence rather than vanishing from every view.

Tests

Around 60 tests added, each verified to fail against the defect it
covers. Includes the DAV cross-account scoping suite, which had no
coverage at all, and replaces two tests that asserted nothing.

patches.title: - tester release README
patches.notes:
Identical code to v0.6.17; this tag exists so the shared release artifact
corresponds to a real commit. Fills in the tester README's contact channel
(issues on the private repository) and its terms (private evaluation build, no
open-source licence applying yet).

patches.title: - delivery-path performance and observability
patches.notes:
Derived search/metadata indexing no longer runs inside the Raft apply path, so
opening a user's index handles cannot block mail delivery.

Raft's LastIndex no longer scans the entire transaction log to find its last
entry. On a log the size of production's this was ~20ms per call against
15.7us for a direct seek, and Raft calls it constantly.

Raft's own logs are no longer discarded. The consensus layer previously ran
completely silent, which made a delivery stall inside it impossible to explain
from the outside.

The delivery stage now reports a per-step breakdown when it is slow, and the
FSM reports slow applies and slow index work.

KNOWN ISSUE: the first delivery after a restart can still take ~70s. Normal
delivery is sub-second (median 0.59s) and warm delivery is ~63ms, so this
affects one message per restart. It is measured to be inside hashicorp/raft
between the write call and our FSM being invoked; see task B12.

patches.title: - derived indexing no longer blocks mail delivery
patches.notes:
The first delivery after a restart took 42-85s, against 63ms once warm,
because the Raft apply maintained per-user search and metadata indexes
inline: the first write paid the cost of opening that user's handles while
the message waited behind it.

Mail and event indexing now runs on a background worker, so a message is
stored and visible immediately and only search catches up fractionally
later. Mailbox listings read from Pebble and are unaffected.

Profile indexing stays inline on purpose, because it writes the shared
system.db that user creation also writes.

Also documents that the 5s passed to the Raft apply is not an upper bound on
the call, sets a SQLite busy timeout, and logs slow index work so a
recurrence reports itself.

patches.title: — trusted submission, scanner wiring, quarantine release fix
patches.notes:
Fixes mail between accounts on a hosted domain being filed as spam: an
authenticated submission (or a connection from a configured trusted network)
is no longer judged by SPF, DKIM alignment and DMARC, which cannot succeed
from a container or LAN address. Content filtering is unchanged — scoring,
Bayes and virus scanning still run for trusted mail.

Fixes a silent mail-loss bug: releasing a message from quarantine moved it to
a spool directory nothing reads, so it was never delivered and never surfaced
again. Release now re-queues it for delivery without re-running the check that
quarantined it.

Wires up scanners that were implemented but never constructed. Enabling
antivirus now actually scans; rspamd and SpamAssassin can be selected and are
composed with the builtin scorer rather than replacing it. An unreachable
antivirus scanner quarantines rather than delivering unscanned (previously it
silently passed everything); an unreachable spam scanner degrades to the
builtin verdict, because mail should never be held up by a spam scanner.

Adds a bulk rescan action so a quarantined backlog can be drained.

Operator note: quarantine is auto-purged after pipeline.quarantine\_retention
(30d default) and the purge deletes the message, so the antivirus recovery
window is finite. Alert on the ERROR log if antivirus is enabled.

patches.title: test, security and CI repair
patches.notes:
Restores a green CI pipeline for the first time since 12 July. Three
independent failures, each masking the next:

- integration: a test scraped a /mail/blob/{hash} URL the app stopped
  emitting after the Phase 9 attachment-dedup work; one failure cascaded
  into a 10-minute suite timeout on CI runners.
- govulncheck: 20 vulnerabilities. 18 stdlib, cleared by moving the go
  directive to 1.26.6; the rest by bumping grpc and x/text.
- gosec: never ran until govulncheck passed. Of three pre-existing HIGH
  findings, the quota-store integer conversions were a real enforcement
  bypass - a negative usage made every storage-quota check pass.

No delivery-path changes since v0.6.13.

patches.title: outbound deliverability
patches.notes:
Fixes outbound SMTP announcing itself as EHLO localhost, which strict
receivers (Postfix reject\_non\_fqdn\_helo\_hostname and most large providers)
permanently rejected - breaking outbound mail from all local users.

Also makes the resulting bounces visible instead of silently junked:
DSNs are DKIM-signed so they pass our own DMARC check, conform to
RFC 3464/3834, and use the null envelope sender. Delivered messages now
carry Authentication-Results and X-Spam-\* headers.
